scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kebyar duduk was created by the Balinese choreographer I Ketut Marya (also known as I Mario) in Tabanan, Bali, and first performed publicly in 1925.
The dance emerged in response to innovations in Balinese gamelan music, specifically gamelan gong kebyar, which featured rapid tempos and sharp dynamic contrasts.
I Mario drew initial inspiration from kebyar legong before developing this distinct interpretative form.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Kebyar duduk is an interpretative dance rather than a narrative story performance.
It is classified as bebancihan (androgynous), occupying a space between refined female (halus) forms and strong male warrior (keras) dances.
In the Balinese classification system, it is categorized as balih-balihan, intended primarily for secular entertainment.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dancer executes virtually all movements while seated, half-seated, or in a cross-legged squatting position.
Holding a fan in the right hand, the dancer spins across the floor in low circles without rising to a full standing posture.
The choreography demands active eye movements that shift rapidly between coquettish, bashful, and angry expressions.
Watch for Angsel, Seated spin.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is set to gamelan gong kebyar music characterized by explosive bursts, dynamic volume shifts, and fast tempos.
A key element of the musical arrangement is the interaction between the lead drummer and the soloist.
Listen for the Gamelan gong kebyar, Kendang (drum), Gongs.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 240 beats a minute.
A dense, metallic orchestral shimmer punctuated by sharp syncopated drum beats and thunderous gong strikes, alternating between sudden silent pauses and fast four-beat-per-second percussive passages.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dancer wears a 5-metre (16 ft) long cloth called a kamben decorated with gold-painted prada patterns.
Accessories and headgear (udeng) feature shimmering golden designs.
The dancer holds a fan in the right hand throughout the performance, using it to complement sharp head and hand gestures.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The creator of the dance is I Ketut Marya (I Mario), a master artist from Tabanan.
Prominent historic performers include his student I Wayan Badra, who performed the piece for Indonesian President Sukarno during the 1950s.
Originating in Tabanan, Bali, the dance spread throughout the island via I Mario's students.
Kebyar duduk evolved from early innovations in gamelan gong kebyar and kebyar legong.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Kebyar duduk is influence of Legong: I Mario drew inspiration from kebyar legong when designing Kebyar duduk.
Kebyar duduk is child of Kebyar trompong: I Mario later expanded Kebyar duduk by incorporating the trompong instrument into a seated performance.
Kebyar duduk is sibling of Oleg tamulilingan: Another famous choreographic creation by I Mario (1952), often paired with Kebyar duduk in performance competitions.

scenes.title: Body and posture
narration: Seated, half-seated, or cross-legged squat with a straight vertical spine held low to the floor
Right hand manipulating a decorative fan with sharp wrist snaps; left arm extending in refined geometric Balinese hand positions
Low center of gravity, rapid lateral torso shifts, and quick spinal turns executed while remaining seated

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Assume a low cross-legged or half-seated squat position on the ground
Step 2: Hold the fan in the right hand and execute sharp wrist flicks

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
